interviewQuestions.question: Design the recommendation system for a video app's homepage.
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd structure this as a funnel, since no single model scores every video for every user in real time. First, **candidate generation**: pull a few hundred plausible videos from multiple sources — a two-tower collaborative model, a content-based match on the user's recent watches, and a trending/popularity pool for cold-start coverage.

Second, **ranking**: score that shortlist with a richer model using dense features — watch-history embeddings, video metadata, time-of-day, device — trained to predict something closer to real value than a raw click, like predicted watch-time completion, since optimizing pure CTR breeds clickbait.

Third, **re-ranking / business rules**: de-duplicate near-identical videos, cap how many videos from one creator appear in a row, inject a small quota of exploratory/novel content, and apply any policy filters.

I'd close on evaluation: validate offline with NDCG and precision@k on held-out data as a cheap first filter, but only trust an A/B test measuring real watch-time and return-visit rate before shipping, since offline and online rankings often disagree.

**Testing:** whether you can structure an open-ended system design answer as a funnel with a labeling choice and an evaluation plan, not just name a model.
